sources.title: Can hysterosalpingo-foam sonography replace hysterosalpingography as first-choice tubal patency test? A randomized non-inferiority trial
sources.claim: 1,026 women had both HyFoSy and HSG; results concordant in 73%; live birth within 12 months 46% (HyFoSy-based) vs 47% (HSG-based); pain 3.1 vs 5.4 on a 0-10 scale; HyFoSy inconclusive 9.5% vs HSG 2.9%.
sources.quote: 1026 women underwent both HyFoSy and HSG ... concordant in 747 women (73%) ... 46% versus 47% ... pain scores HyFoSy 3.1 (SD 2.2) and HSG 5.4 (SD 2.5)

sources.title: Oil-Based or Water-Based Contrast for Hysterosalpingography in Infertile Women
sources.claim: 1,119 women randomized; ongoing pregnancy 39.7% with oil-based vs 29.1% with water-based contrast.
sources.quote: A total of 1119 women were randomly assigned ... 220 of 554 women in the oil group (39.7%) and 161 of 554 women in the water group (29.1%) had an ongoing pregnancy
sources.checked_with: WebFetch Maastricht University research record (abstract) 2026-10-18; NEJM and PubMed pages refused

sources.title: Fertility evaluation of infertile women: a committee opinion
sources.claim: HSG documents tubal occlusion and shows the uterine cavity; bilateral proximal blockage on HSG needs further evaluation to exclude artifact; HyCoSy sensitivity 76-96%, specificity 67-100%; laparoscopy not recommended routinely for tubal patency.
sources.quote: findings suggesting bilateral proximal tubal obstruction require further evaluation to exclude the possibility of an artifact ... The sensitivity of hysterosalpingo-contrast sonography for the determination of tubal patency ranges from 76%-96% ... Laparoscopy is not recommended as a routine method for assessing tubal patency.

sources.title: Hysterosalpingosonography for diagnosing tubal occlusion in subfertile women: a systematic review with meta-analysis
sources.claim: 28 studies, 1,551 women; in 9 head-to-head studies vs laparoscopy, sono-HSG sensitivity 95% / specificity 93% and HSG 94% / 92%; performs similarly to HSG.
sources.quote: Sono-HSG: sensitivity 0.95, specificity 0.93; HSG: sensitivity 0.94, specificity 0.92 ... sono-HSG is an accurate test for diagnosing tubal occlusion and performs similarly to HSG

sources.title: Are patient characteristics associated with the accuracy of hysterosalpingography in diagnosing tubal pathology? An individual patient data meta-analysis
sources.claim: 4,521 women in 7 studies: HSG sensitivity 53% and specificity 87% for any tubal pathology; 46% and 95% for bilateral pathology.
sources.quote: We acquired data of seven primary studies containing data of 4521 women ... Pooled sensitivity and specificity of HSG were 53% and 87% for any tubal pathology
sources.checked_with: WebFetch University of Aberdeen research record (abstract) 2026-10-18

sources.title: Hysterosalpingogram (HSG) patient fact sheet
sources.claim: HSG is done after the period ends and before ovulation, takes under 5 minutes, causes mild or moderate cramping for about 5-10 minutes; complications occur less than 1% of the time; radiation is very low.
sources.quote: usually takes less than 5 minutes to perform ... mild or moderate uterine cramping for about 5-10 minutes ... occur less than 1% of the time ... Radiation exposure from an HSG is very low

sources.title: Hysterosalpingo-foam sonography versus hysterosalpingography during fertility work-up: an economic evaluation alongside a randomized controlled trial
sources.claim: Procedure cost HyFoSy EUR 136 vs HSG EUR 280 in the Dutch trial; estimated live birth 46% vs 47%.
sources.quote: For the procedures itself, HyFoSy cost EUR136 and HSG EUR280 ... the estimated chance of live birth was 46% after HyFoSy versus 47% after HSG
